extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners; patent practitioners/prosecuting attorneys
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and substantive criteria for issuing, responding to, and treating requirements for information under 37 CFR 1.105 (and related Patentability Report practice) during patent prosecution and related proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to combine requirement for information with first action
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement for information may be combined with a first action on the merits that includes at least one rejection if the application file or the lack of relevant prior art found in the examiner's search justifies asking the applicant if he or she has information that would be relevant to the patentability determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not appropriate to make a requirement for information based on a lack of relevant prior art with a first action on the merits allowance or Ex parte Quayle action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of requirements after first action on the merits
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement for information made after the first action on the merits may be appropriate when the application file justifies asking the applicant if he or she has information relevant to patentability, but it is rarely appropriate to require information because of a lack of relevant prior art after the first action on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A requirement for information is not proper when no further action would be taken by the examiner; reasonable necessity implies further action by the examiner, so requirements for information generally should be in non-final actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited circumstances for issuing requirements in issued/abandoned applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Under limited circumstances, requirements under 37 CFR 1.105 may be made in an application that is issued or abandoned, normally only during part of some ongoing proceeding involving the issued patent or abandoned application (e.g., proceedings to revive an abandoned application, or proceedings to change inventorship and reexamination proceedings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: requests in abandoned applications during revival proceedings; requests in patents during inventorship change proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and completeness of replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies to requirements for information must be complete and filed within the time period set including any extensions; failure to reply within the time period will result in abandonment of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All replies should be checked for completeness. Any incomplete reply can be completed within the original time period including extensions. Supplemental replies filed after expiration must comply with all other rules for submissions of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship of 37 CFR 1.105 to duty of disclosure (37 CFR 1.56)
rubrics_metrics.description: The duty of candor under 37 CFR 1.56 applies to applicant’s reply to a 1.105 requirement and requires that applicant reply with information reasonably and readily available. 37 CFR 1.56's threshold (material to patentability) is substantially higher than the 1.105 threshold (reasonable necessity to examination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike 1.56 (no duty to search for unknown info), 1.105 requires submission of information already known but does not require searching for unknown information. Information required under 1.105 may not be considered material to patentability by applicant but is reasonably necessary to determine state of the art, context, directions of the art, similarity to other art, or to proceed in examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: What constitutes a complete reply to a 1.105 requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete reply is a reply to each enumerated requirement giving either the information required or a statement that the information required is unknown and/or not readily available to the party or parties from which it was requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No requirement to show that the required information was not in fact readily attainable, but applicant must make a good faith attempt and reasonable inquiry. A reply stating unknown or not readily available will generally be sufficient unless it is clear applicant did not understand the requirement or the reply was ambiguous and a more specific answer is possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of an incomplete reply
rubrics_metrics.description: An incomplete reply to a 37 CFR 1.105 requirement in a pending application or reexamination proceeding is handled like an amendment not fully responsive to a non-final office action (see 37 CFR 1.135(c) and MPEP § 714.03).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the reply is bona fide, form paragraph 7.95 may be used. This practice does not apply where there has been a deliberate omission of necessary parts, or where the application is subject to a final Office action (examiner has no authority to grant an extension if period for reply has expired). In abandoned applications, an incomplete reply terminates the proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time periods for reply to 1.105 requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Time for reply to a 1.105 requirement is governed by 37 CFR 1.135 and 1.136. Requirements made without an action on the merits should set a shortened statutory period of two months for reply; applicant may extend up to six months under 1.136(a). Requirements sent with an office action use the same period as the action on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A requirement for information under 1.105 is an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 for patent term adjustment purposes (see MPEP § 2730).

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle for making a requirement for information
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement for information under 37 CFR 1.105 should be narrowly specified and limited in scope because it is a significant burden on both the applicant and the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A requirement is only warranted where the benefit from the information exceeds the burden in obtaining that information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and content of the requirement (must state basis and form)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement must clearly indicate that a requirement under 37 CFR 1.105 is being made, the basis for the requirement, and the specific information being required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements should specify the particular art area involved, the particular claimed subject matter within such art area, and the form the required information is expected to take (citations/copies of individual art references, identification of collections, answers to questions, or other specified form). Preferably prepare the requirement as a separate document to call attention and facilitate routing within applicant's organization. The requirement should state why it has been made and how the information is necessary to examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.105 (Requirement for Information, Heading)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use form paragraph 7.105 at the beginning of any requirement under 37 CFR 1.105: 'Applicant and the assignee of this application are required under 37 CFR 1.105 to provide the following information that the examiner has determined is reasonably necessary to the examination of this application.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow 7.105 with explanation of why required info is necessary; use appropriate subsequent form paragraphs (7.106–7.121) and concluding paragraphs (7.122–7.126) as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.106 (Domain of Search)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use when the information is required to extend the domain of search for prior art: identify class and subclasses and describe why a broader range of art is needed to establish the level of knowledge of those of ordinary skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.122–7.126 as appropriate; insert description of art claimed but not fully represented in Office collections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.107 (Level of Skill and Knowledge in the Art)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request information required to document the level of skill and knowledge in the relevant art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.122–7.126 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.108 (Background Description)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request information required to complete the background description in the disclosure by documenting specified aspects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.122–7.126 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.109 (Products and Services Embodying Invention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request identification of products and services embodying the disclosed subject matter and properties of similar products/services found in prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.122–7.126 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.110 (Art Suggested as Relevant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request the art suggested by the applicant as relevant to the examination and where in the application file that suggestion appears.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.122–7.126 as appropriate; describe where applicant suggests the art is relevant (specification page, paper received date, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.111 (List of Keywords)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request a list of keywords particularly helpful in locating publications related to the disclosed art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.122–7.126 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.112 (Citations for Databases or Indexed Collections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request citations to electronically searchable databases or other indexed collections containing publications documenting knowledge within the disclosed art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.122–7.126 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.113 (Copy of Art Referred to in Disclosure but Not Submitted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request copies of items of art that are referred to in the disclosure but not previously submitted to the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify where applicant refers to such art (specification page or paper received date); must be preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.122–7.126.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.114 (Copies of Publications Authored by Inventors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request copies of each publication authored or co-authored by any applicant that describe the disclosed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.122–7.126 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.115 (Art Relied Upon for Description of Prior Art)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request title, citation and copy of each publication that is a source used for the description of the prior art in the disclosure, with a concise explanation of that publication's contribution to the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited to documents actually relied on (not all documents believed relevant); must be preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.122–7.126.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.116 (Art Relied Upon for Development of Invention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request title, citation and copy of each publication any applicant relied upon to develop the disclosed subject matter, with concise explanation of the reliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited to documents actually relied on; insert description of most important inventive elements in bracket 1; must be preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.122–7.126.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.117 (Art Relied Upon for Drafting Claimed Subject Matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request title, citation and copy of each publication any applicant relied upon in drafting the claimed subject matter, with explanation of reliance in distinguishing claims from prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited to documents actually relied on; must be preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.122–7.126.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.118 (Results of Applicant’s Prior Art Search)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request whether any prior art search was performed, citations for each prior art collection searched, and citations/copies of art considered material to demonstrating the knowledge of a person having ordinary skill in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.122–7.126; describe subject matter for which art is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.119 & 7.120 (Names of Products or Services Incorporating Claimed/Disclosed Art)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request names of any products or services that have incorporated the claimed subject matter (7.119) or the disclosed prior art (7.120).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.122–7.126; for prior art, specify attributes that most closely approximate the claimed subject matter to narrow focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.121 (Details of Improvement Over the Prior Art)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request statement of specific improvements of claimed subject matter over disclosed prior art and indicate specific elements providing those improvements; for means/steps-plus-function claims provide page and line numbers describing the claimed structure and acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.122–7.126.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.122 (Submission of Only Pertinent Pages)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where large documents are requested, the requirement may be met by providing copies of only those pages that provide the particular subject matter indicated in the requirement (or that subject matter found in applicant's disclosure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use where scope specifically includes citations/copies of publications; follow with form paragraphs regarding waiver and reply content as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.123 (Waiver of Fee and Statement Requirements for Initial Replies)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee and certification requirements of 37 CFR 1.97 are waived for those documents submitted in reply to a 1.105 requirement that are included in the applicant's first complete communication responding to the requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver extends only to documents within the scope of the requirement included in the first complete communication. Supplemental replies and information beyond the scope are subject to the fee and certification requirements of 1.97 where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.124 (Contents of Good Faith Reply)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reply must be made with candor and good faith under 37 CFR 1.56; where applicant does not have or cannot readily obtain an item, a statement that the item is unknown or cannot be readily obtained will be accepted as a complete reply for that item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.105 and followed by 7.125 or 7.126 as appropriate; include as conclusion of any requirement for information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs 7.125–7.127 (Conclusions/Time Period Statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶7.125: Conclusion when requirement accompanies an Office action — time for reply coincides with time for the Office action. ¶7.126: Conclusion when requirement mailed without any other Office action — subject to 1.134, 1.135, 1.136 and short statutory period of [1] months (ordinarily 2 months). ¶7.127: Use when scope specifically includes copies of publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert appropriate period (ordinarily 2 months) and indicate extension availability under 1.136(a); 7.127 used where copies of publications are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's obligation to consider applicant's reply
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must consider the information submitted with the applicant's reply and apply the information as the examiner deems appropriate; identification of areas of search must be considered and the examiner must indicate which areas were used and which were not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indications may be placed in file wrapper search notes or by notations on applicant's reply with initials/date. Answers to queries must be considered with a record indicating 'Considered' and initials/date. Art submitted in response must be considered at least to the extent that IDS under 1.97/1.98 is considered. If applicant provides a written list of citations, examiner must indicate which art has been considered; if applicant provides no list, examiner need not prepare one unless relying on such art in a rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of consideration for submissions in reply
rubrics_metrics.description: It is never appropriate to deny considering information submitted in reply that is within the scope of the 1.105 requirement. Information beyond the scope need not be considered unless submission conforms to 1.97/1.98 and MPEP § 609.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope of 1.105 requirement measured by the plain meaning of the text of the requirement; therefore scope must be carefully specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to modify or withdraw a 1.105 requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants seeking withdrawal/modification of a 1.105 requirement or to have information considered may submit a petition under 37 CFR 1.181 to the Director of the Technology Center where the requirement was issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition is not a reply to the requirement — the reply time period continues to run even if a petition has been submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation of 1.105 replies to disclosure statement rules (1.97/1.98)
rubrics_metrics.description: An initial reply responsive to the requirement and submitted within the original time period does not have to satisfy fee and/or certification requirements of 1.97/1.98; applicant should list references on Form PTO-1449 or PTO/SB/08 to have citations entered in the record; submissions beyond the scope of the requirement are submissions under 1.97/1.98 and must meet those provisions to be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where information is submitted in reply to a 1.105 requirement, the examiner may NOT make the next Office action relying on that art final unless all instances of application of such art are necessitated by amendment — distinguishes practice from submissions under 1.97/1.98.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to request a Patentability Report (P.R.)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application assigned to one Technology Center contains one or more claims classifiable in one or more other TCs (claims not divisible inter se), the application may be referred to the other TC(s) for a Patentability Report as to certain designated claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The forwarding TC should send a memorandum such as 'For Patentability Report from TC -- as to claims --.' Use P.R. practice only in extraordinary circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and disposition of a Patentability Report
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patentability Report is a memorandum including citation of all pertinent references and a complete action on all claims involved; the field of search covered should be endorsed on the file wrapper by the reporting examiner; when signed by the primary examiner in the reporting TC it is returned to the TC of original assignment and placed in the file wrapper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner preparing the P.R. may receive an explanation from the assigned examiner to avoid duplication. The report, if legibly written, need not be typed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling disagreements about classification or patentability reports
rubrics_metrics.description: If disagreement as to classification arises, it may be referred to a patent classifier. If the primary examiner in the TC having jurisdiction does not agree with the P.R., they may consult the reporting primary examiner; if no agreement is reached the jurisdictional primary examiner may make their own action and remove the P.R. from the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: P.R. practice is to be used only where it will save total examiner time or improve quality; if primary examiner agrees with P.R., incorporate substance in action; P.R. then remains in file until final disposal and is then removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals involving claims examinable in reporting TC
rubrics_metrics.description: When an appeal is taken from rejection of claims all examinable in the TC preparing a P.R., and the application is otherwise allowable, formal transfer of the application to that TC should be made for appeal purposes; the receiving TC will take jurisdiction and prepare the examiner's answer; at allowance the application may be sent to issue by that TC with classification determined by controlling claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use formal transfer to receive jurisdiction for appeal-only purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence of examination when multiple TCs involved
rubrics_metrics.description: If supervisory patent examiners cannot agree as to order of examination by their TCs, the supervisory PE having jurisdiction will direct a complete search of the art relevant to his/her claims prior to referring the application to another TC for report; the referred TC will be advised of search results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If supervisors think a different sequence is expedient, modify the order of search accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting and recording Patentability Reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Forwarding an application for a P.R. is not to be treated as a transfer by the forwarding TC; when P.R. completed and application returned it is not counted as receipt or action by transfer, but credit is given for time spent. Date status in reporting TC determined on basis of dates in TC of original jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide timely reminders to the TC making the P.R. to ensure orderly progress in reported dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate prints of drawings for P.R. and post-prosecution notification
rubrics_metrics.description: In P.R. applications having drawings, assigned examiner will furnish prints of applicable drawing sheets to reporting TC for interference search purposes and note that this has been done. When application that had P.R. prosecution is passed for issue or becomes abandoned, notify each TC that submitted a P.R.; examiners note date of allowance/abandonment on duplicate prints; prints may be destroyed when of no value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate provision of duplicate prints by pencil notation on file wrapper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on use of Patentability Report practice
rubrics_metrics.description: P.R. practice is not obligatory and should be resorted to only where it will save total examiner time or result in improved quality due to specialized knowledge. Where claims are directed to the same character of invention but differ in scope only, P.R. is never proper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemplary situations where P.R. ordinarily is not proper: (A) claims related as manufacturing process and a product defined by the process; (B) claims related as product and a process which merely makes the product having certain characteristics; (C) claims related as a combination distinguished solely by characteristics of a subcombination and such subcombination per se. Where P.R. will save total examiner time it is permitted with Director approval (stamp 'Approved' required).
